adjudication.rationale: After directly reading the entire actual relevance-rubric.md and protocol.md and rereading every actual original a079/39031 projected field, I revise my earlier title-based uncertainty. Trials is not inherently physical: computer simulations can comprise trials and have recorded outputs. The title contains no explicit physical/field/sample/empirical qualification, unlike the stronger field-notes cue formerly present in a different seed. Here the first description sentence explicitly establishes that all entries are computer simulations and no physical trial or empirical observations were collected. A later sentence labels the three columns simulated, and both CSV and JSON descriptions independently begin Simulated output columns. The generic Recorded series and Study records distribution titles also do not claim physical collection. The nominal observed-spoilage column name is within that simulation qualification and is not evidence that spoilage was empirically observed. The frozen rubric requires representative measurements for the semantic intent and treats simulation-only basis as a decisive mismatch; it does not define the bare word trials as necessarily empirical. Reading the complete metadata therefore supports one coherent simulation-only interpretation without an unresolved factual contradiction. This is a reasoned reconsideration of the same text, not a claim that the title was repaired, and not a forced empirical positive. All simulated output facts remain explicitly distinguished from empirical measurements; no measurement or relevance grade is manufactured.
